A-r1.verdict: USED as concept-A.png (grade.py k 1.5). flux-2 invented a wall socket on the right wall above the skirting (left in A; inpainted in B's input) and a planter and gravel court outside the glass; the rug came out as a beige flat weave with a border, the lumbar cushion in white boucle
A-r1.prompt:
Turn the attached image into ONE real photograph: an editorial interior photograph for a luxury design magazine. The attached image is a rough computer layout of this exact living room with the real furniture and products already in place. Keep the camera, the framing and the place, size, shape and colour of every object exactly as drawn. Re-photograph all of it together in one natural light so that nothing looks pasted: every object stands in the room's own light, with soft real contact shadows where it touches the floor, the rug, the sofa or the wall, with true materials, depth and air between things.

LIGHT: a winter afternoon, about 15:00, with NO direct sun: soft, even, cool-neutral daylight (4600 K) from the glazing on the left, no sun patch and no hard shadow anywhere in the room. The exposure is held half a stop low, so the daylight stays quiet and the four lamps carry the picture. All four lamps are switched ON, warm 2700 K: the two wall lights wash the plaster gently up and down and frame the three prints, the floor lamp's shade glows and drops a pool of light on the sofa's right arm and the throw, the pendant glows softly over the table. Their warm pools are the brightest things in the room, against soft, quiet shade on the plaster. Outside the glazing: a small walled garden with an olive tree in soft, shadowless daylight.

THE ROOM: a warm-minimal Mediterranean living room. Bone-white limewash plaster walls with a soft hand-trowelled movement; a matte smoked-oak plank floor; on the left, tall slim dark-bronze steel glazing and a low limestone window bench.

IN IT, exactly as drawn and nothing more: a large natural ivory braided-wool rug with fine ribs. A greige boucle sofa, monolithic and soft, with wide rounded arms and a rounded back on a recessed walnut plinth; on it a caramel ribbed corduroy cushion on the left, a sand linen lumbar cushion and a taupe boucle cushion on the right, and a pecan-brown waffle cotton throw slipping from the right arm to the seat corner. THE COFFEE TABLE: one thin slab of light natural oak, matte oiled, that rolls over both short ends in a soft bend and runs to the floor as two flat slab legs, completely open underneath; on it two small travertine candle holders with ivory pillar candles and one low matte black bowl. On the wall, three abstract prints in slim walnut frames (cream, caramel, espresso, warm grey) between two small travertine cylinder wall lights. Right of the sofa, a floor lamp: slim walnut-and-brass stem, white pleated cone shade. Over the table, a three-tier ivory linen drum pendant on a thin cord, whole inside the frame with plaster above it. On the left: a young olive tree with a slender grey trunk in a ribbed sand-coloured cement pot, a tall woven jute basket with two handles, a white textured stoneware vase with one dry olive branch on the window bench, and, in the foreground, cut by the frame, an armchair with an oiled walnut frame and bone boucle cushions. At the bottom edge, the top of a black metal-tube magazine holder.

CAMERA: 35 mm lens at 1.05 m, level, verticals straight, f/5.6: the sofa wall sharp, the armchair in the foreground slightly soft. Fine natural film grain; rich deep walnut and espresso tones; every finish matte.

DO NOT add or change anything: no extra furniture, no side table, no books, no flowers, no other plants, no extra lamps, no ceiling spots, no curtain, no mirror, no TV, no people, no text. The coffee table is never dark, never walnut, never on round drum or pedestal legs.

B-r1.verdict: NOT USED (kept in raw/): the sun, the leaf shadow, the Olia's form and the whole pendant are right, but the sofa came out with square track arms in a flat weave (not the rounded-arm boucle sofa), the planter as a wicker basket (the Bible's rejection list), a book and a pen invented under the bowl, and the plaster as rough stucco

Keep this photograph exactly as it is: the same room, the same camera and framing, the same furniture and objects, each in its place, size, shape, material and colour. Change only the light, and make that light physically real, so the picture reads as one photograph taken at this moment.

LIGHT: the last low sun of a winter afternoon, warm gold, comes through the glazing on the left, as the image already sketches: a long warm patch of sunlight on the plaster wall behind the sofa and on the left part of the sofa and its caramel cushion, crossed by the soft straight shadows of the glazing bars, and the olive tree's soft, lacy leaf shadow on the plaster between the left wall light and the first print. Photograph that sunlight for real: the sunlit plaster glows and is the brightest thing in the picture, the shadow edges are soft, warm light bounces from the sunlit wall onto the sofa, the rug and the oak table, and every object keeps a soft contact shadow. The rest of the room rests in soft warm shade. All the lamps stay switched ON, warm 2700 K: the two wall lights wash the plaster gently up and down, the floor lamp's pleated shade glows and lights the sofa's right arm and the throw, the pendant glows softly over the table. Outside the glazing: the garden olive tree in back light under a pale gold sky.

KEEP UNCHANGED: the greige boucle sofa with its rounded arms; THE COFFEE TABLE, one thin slab of light natural oak that bends over both short ends into two flat slab legs, open underneath, with only the two travertine candle holders and the one matte black bowl on it; the caramel ribbed cushion, the pale lumbar cushion, the taupe boucle cushion and the pecan-brown throw; the three abstract prints in slim walnut frames between the two travertine wall lights; the floor lamp with its white pleated shade; the three-tier ivory linen pendant, whole inside the frame with plaster above it; the olive tree in its ribbed sand-coloured cement pot; the woven jute basket; the white vase with its dry branch; the armchair with the walnut frame and bone boucle cushions; the black magazine holder; the natural ivory wool rug; the smoked-oak floor.

The walls are smooth, matte, bone-white limewash with only the faintest soft movement: no rough stucco, no trowel ridges.

Editorial interior photograph for a luxury design magazine: 35 mm lens, level camera, straight verticals, fine natural grain, rich deep walnut tones, every finish matte.
